messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected on prod-gateway (us-east-1). Current 5xx: 18% over 5m, baseline ~0.3%. Request rate steady. Trigger: gateway-error-rate > 5%
alyssa: seeing same in the dashboard, lots of 502 and 504, spike started ~10:02 UTC. Correlates with increased kv-cache misses on the edge.
omar: logs are sparse — several spans missing request_id header, traces not linking. I can only see LB-level metrics. Looks like tracing sampler dropped or header propagation broke.
sre-oncall: paging oncall now. @maya you up? can you take first response?
maya: oncall here. grabbing traces/metrics. any customer-facing alerts?
cs-rep: CS reported a handful of API failures from a couple of enterprise customers (retryable 5xx). They asked if there was any ETA.
leo: I can temporarily route traffic away from the failing pool. Which nodes are noisy?
alyssa: edge pool a-2 and a-3 show high tail latency and 502s. Same version deployed earlier today.
omar: I tried fetching traces via the tracing UI but span IDs absent for many requests. stack: edge -> gateway -> model-proxy. Missing req-id seems to originate at edge proxy.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Recent deploy to gateway-service v2.14.8 at 09:58 UTC by @ci. (sha abc123). Rollback available.
maya: let's do quick containment: 1) add short-term debug headers on edge to force request-id injection 2) route traffic off a-2/a-3 3) enable higher trace sampling for 1m 4) notify customers. I'll coordinate.
alyssa: command to add debug header on edge (nginx):
```
kubectl -n infra exec deploy/edge-proxy -- /bin/sh -c "sed -i 's/proxy_set_header X-Request-Id .*/proxy_set_header X-Request-Id $request_id;/' /etc/nginx/conf.d/proxy.conf && nginx -s reload"
```
leo: routing change underway: shifting 25% of traffic away from pool a-2/a-3 to b-pool. rolling out now.
sre-oncall: maya — handing pager to you. full handoff: observed 5xx spike, missing trace headers at edge, possible recent gateway deploy, initial mitigation: partial traffic shift + debug header injection.
maya: taking it. I'll also hit quick telemetry probes: enabling trace sampling to 50% for 10m and toggling verbose request logging for gateway-service.
omar: adding a short-lived logging shim to inject request_id when missing. pushing config now. snippet:
```
# python middleware pseudocode
if not req.headers.get('X-Request-Id'):
    req.headers['X-Request-Id'] = uuid4().hex
    logger.info('injected-reqid', path=req.path)
```
alyssa: deployed shim to staging; pushing to prod in canary mode (5% traffic). need logs to verify.
infra-bot: metric: trace-sample-rate set to 0.5 for service=gateway-service (api).
leo: traffic shift completed: a-2/a-3 at 0%. b-pool moved to absorb. Observed immediate drop in 5xx rate from 18% -> 9% on b-pool, a-2 still at 22% (isolated).
cs-rep: letting customers know: sending brief note — investigating, mitigation in progress, ETA 30m.
maya: requesting short-term instrumentation: add an ad-hoc log line at edge to capture upstream status and response body for 502s. We'll keep it for 20m. Any objections?
sre-oncall: fine for 20m. watch cost.
omar: logs are starting to show injected reqids — tracing UI beginning to link a few requests. Still missing for many older requests.
alyssa: discovered repeated upstream error from model-proxy: "upstream read timeout" and repeated header truncation. Could be connection pool exhaustion.
leo: scaling model-proxy pool by +30% now and increasing connection_pool size. Command: `kubectl scale deployment model-proxy --replicas=13 -n runtime`
maya: scaling done, connection_pool bumped. Also opening temporary circuit-breaker rule to fail fast for slow backends to reduce head-of-line.
infra-bot: alert-suppression: incident-bot alerts temporarily throttled for gateway-service to prevent noisy alerts.
omar: quick check: with injected reqids, we see 3 customer requests that hit 502 chain: edge->gateway->model-proxy and model-proxy logs show "connection reset by peer" at 10:19 UTC. That points to downstream DB or cache.
alyssa: kv-cache (redis) latency jump coincides at 10:17. Ops, that's likely the root for the chain.
leo: paging redis-oncall. @leo -> pinging infra ops to confirm any maintenance.
leo: redis team confirms transient failover event around 10:16 that produced elevated latencies. They fixed primary; replicas catching up.
cs-rep: customers asking if any requests were dropped permanently — some retries succeeded, a few saw errors. We'll coordinate postmortem messaging.
maya: current state summary: traffic routed off bad nodes, model-proxy scaled, connection_pool increased, request-id injections and trace sampling increased, ad-hoc verbose logs for 502s enabled. 5xx rate down to 4.2% cluster-wide. still watching.
sre-oncall: agree. start preparing a short incident post with timeline and customer impact. assign owners: timeline & cause — @alyssa; remediation steps — @leo; observability gaps/next steps — @omar; customer comms — @cs-rep.
alyssa: noted. quick note: we had an observability gap because request-id injection is not enforced at edge; tracing sampling default is low; and our runbook didn't include kv-cache failover trace points.
omar: follow-ups: 1) add enforced req-id at ingress 2) increase baseline trace sampling during deploys 3) small playbook for redis failover -> gateway cascade 4) short-term: ensure escaped logs include upstream status and response body for 502s (masked PII).
maya: agreed. I'll stay on for the next 30m to monitor then update the incident channel.
cs-rep: I sent customers an update: short outage window, mitigation in place, we will follow up once root cause confirmed.
alyssa: closing loop: last check 10:42 UTC 5xx cluster 1.1%. will keep monitoring for 30m and then mark incident as resolved if stable.
incident-bot: Incident interim update saved to incident tracker: https://incidents.redwood.dev/INC-2026-447890 (assigned: maya, severity: P2).
maya: thanks team. postmortem owners please add docs. I'll create a short timeline and action items in the runbook.
leo: holding on redis team follow-up to confirm their mitigations and any next steps for kv-cache HA.
omar: will draft the observability taks. putting a ticket to enforce req-id at ingress and improve trace sampling toggles.
alyssa: great work all — quick and coordinated. :thumbsup:
